text:
jordan-acme: Hi team, since we shifted traffic to rwdl-large-v2 yesterday, our assistant started omitting the mandated system header after long contexts (~8k tokens). Example: we include 'Always prepend LEGAL_HEADER' in system, but responses no longer include it in long sessions. Rolling back to v1 fixed it. This is blocking production for us. Request id: abc123, timestamp 2026-03-15T18:22:11Z.

sara-support: Thanks Jordan — sorry for the disruption. Can you paste the exact API call you used and the request_id? cc @alex-eng-runtime @jun-oncall

jordan-acme: Here's the curl we used, trimmed for clarity:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"rwdl-large-v2","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"Always prepend LEGAL_HEADER:"},{"role":"user","content":"<very long conversation ~9k tokens>"}],"max_tokens":1024}'
```

request_id: abc123

alex-eng-runtime: I pulled request abc123 from traces. Model: rwdl-large-v2-quant (selector path). At ~8200 tokens we see repeated kv_cache_evict logs and then a short-circuit in the prefix-preserve stage. Pasting relevant log lines:

```
[2026-03-15T18:22:10.123Z] kv_cache_len=8196 kv_cache_evict=true evict_seq=8192
[2026-03-15T18:22:10.124Z] prefix_preserve: tokens_kept=64 tokens_dropped=8096
[2026-03-15T18:22:10.125Z] policy_check: system_header_found=false -> dropping header
```

jun-oncall: I repro'd locally with the same prompt and model binary. Confirmed: system header gets dropped once the sequence crosses a quantization boundary (around 8k tokens for this cluster config). Also observed a latency increase (~40%) in that region; could indicate switching to a slower attention kernel then triggering an eviction path.

sara-support: Customer is blocked. Jordan, would you like us to route your traffic back to rwdl-large-v1 immediately while we investigate? We can do a targeted traffic shift for your org.

jordan-acme: Yes please switch back now. We cannot serve responses missing the legal header (regulatory reasons). Please confirm when done and share RCA timeline.

alex-eng-runtime: Executing traffic shift for org:acme -> rwdl-large-v1 (95% traffic). Command run: `infractl traffic shift --org acme --from rwdl-large-v2 --to rwdl-large-v1 --pct 95 --note "rollback long-context regression"`

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Traffic shift executed: rollout_id=r-20260315-77 org=acme from=rwdl-large-v2 to=rwdl-large-v1 pct=95 status=done

jun-oncall: For reproducibility, here's a minimal repro script that still triggers the drop (replace API key):

```python
import requests
headers={"Authorization":"Bearer sk_xxx","Content-Type":"application/json"}
data={"model":"rwdl-large-v2","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"Always prepend LEGAL_HEADER:"},{"role":"user","content":"A"*9000}],"max_tokens":256}
r=requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate',json=data,headers=headers)
print(r.status_code, r.json().get('choices'))
```

alex-eng-runtime: Filed INF-4521 (internal): "rwdl-large-v2: prefix preservation fails after kv cache eviction / quant boundary". Assigning to eng-ml. Attaching traces and logs from abc123. @maria-eng-ml tagging you for kernel + quant path review.

maria-eng-ml: Thanks — initial hypothesis: an off-by-one when selecting the attention kernel fallback after quantized matmul path changes token window bookkeeping. I need the exact model binary checksum and the canary traffic coverage details.

jun-oncall: Checksum: sha256:deadbeefcafebabefeedface0000000000000000000000000000000000000000. Canary coverage was ~3% traffic for v2 at deploy time; long sessions were rare in canary so it didn't surface.

sara-support: Jordan, rollback to v1 is complete on our side. Can you validate in prod and confirm within 30m? We'll follow up with a timeline and keep you updated on the fix.

jordan-acme: Confirmed — behavior back to expected. Thank you for the fast rollback. Please escalate to engineering and share ETA for a proper fix; this affected legal compliance in two customer-facing flows.
